A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Zero-Inflated Bandits by the same authors. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original MAB and contextual-bandit simulations, evaluation using loan records, and supplementary numerical analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations, loan-record evaluation and supplementary numerical analyses, now in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The contextual procedures are substantively revised. v2 Algorithm 5's residual-norm optimizations become feature-weighted estimating equations in Algorithm B.3, with corrected covariance dimensions and time-dependent exploration radii. Algorithm B.4 scores products of sampled linear predictors, whereas v2's TS template applies the reward link functions before multiplying. The MAB procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Gaussian, Gaussian-mixture and exponential simulations, sparsity and rare-reward scenarios, and auto-loan dataset. The newly discussed infinite-action setting is theoretical; no corresponding evaluation is added.

E2.justification: The MAB comparisons retain the four UCB baselines based on non-zero-part, variance, estimated-proxy and true-proxy parameters, plus MOTS. The contextual and loan comparisons retain misspecified and integrated UCB/TS baselines.

E3.justification: The contextual-UCB experiments refer to the algorithm appendix for tuning; those referenced settings change from fixed radii in Assumption A.3 to round-dependent radii in Assumption B.3. Other reported experimental budgets and settings remain unchanged. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The supplementary analyses of non-zero probabilities, contextual sparsity, loan-model specifications, noise sensitivity and variance-proxy behavior are retained. No new ablation, robustness experiment or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Both report 50 MAB replications and 25 contextual replications, with identical plotted error bars. No new seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice or significance test is disclosed.

E6.justification: Figures 1-10 retain identical plotted content, and Table 2 retains all FDR values. The empirical rankings and findings are unchanged; the revised theoretical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 adds the asymptotic lower-bound analysis in Lemma 6.1 and its proof, revises the contextual-UCB bound and proof, and introduces the explicit contextual-TS guarantee in Corollary B.4. It removes v2 Corollary 1 and its proof comparing product concentration and regret bounds against standard UCB. The heavy-tailed theorem is retained as Theorem A.2, rather than removed.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion broaden the stated contextual-theory contribution beyond UCB to include TS, and Section 4.2 explicitly claims applicability to countably infinite action spaces. The central zero-inflated modeling contribution and empirical-superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: The expanded discussion explicitly identifies asymptotic order-optimality as unproved and suggests allocating confidence probabilities according to non-zero probabilities as future work. Separately, Section 2 changes the explanation of loose confidence bounds from over-exploration to under-exploration, reversing that mechanism statement.

D1.justification: v3 expands and revises the contextual implementation specification through explicit estimating equations, covariance matrices, exploration-radius formulas and GLM-TS pseudocode. Hardware, simulation-time disclosures, loan-data processing and dataset-access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on doubling tricks, asymptotic optimality and mathematical analysis, including Besson and Kaufmann and Lai and Robbins, while removing several contextual-TS and concentration references. The main positioning relative to semiparametric, hierarchical and bootstrap bandits is retained.

P1.justification: The main text and appendices are substantially reorganized: heavy-tailed material moves into Appendix A, the contextual exposition and theory are rewritten and expanded, and the discussion gains an optimality subsection. The abstract is rewritten, an impact statement is added, and theorem, equation and appendix numbering is reorganized.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned around minimax ratios, with a contextual-TS row and explanatory footnotes. The main Algorithm 2 display changes to UCB, and a separate GLM-TS algorithm block is added. Figures and tables are relocated, but the underlying plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies contextual algorithm specifications and explicitly discusses unproved optimality. However, its new Lemma 6.1 displays a lower bound that evaluates to zero for suboptimal positive-mean arms, undermining the stated optimality conclusion. Corollary B.4 also gives TS an extra dimension factor despite Section 4.2 claiming the same rate as UCB. These substantive inconsistencies coexist with useful clarification, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
